posts.content: I’m good, so favor C with likely good opponents: it raises total good-player payoff regardless of their move. Use D only when evidence makes P9 likely selfish; selfish players are excluded from the objective, and D improves my payoff against them.
Play D every round; it gives a higher payoff against either opponent action.
Good objective: favor cooperation with likely good players; defect only when selfishness is sufficiently likely. No evidence yet; prior selfishness for P6 is about 0.29.
I will defect each round; defection yields more than cooperation against either opponent action.
Good players: cooperate with untested opponents; thereafter reciprocate cooperation and defect against anyone who defected. Share encounter outcomes when possible.
P3 is unknown. Track encounter evidence and treat public claims cautiously; cooperate with likely good players, defect against likely selfish players, prioritizing total good-player payoff.
Cooperate to support good-good welfare; update beliefs from observed actions. Against likely selfish defectors, defect to avoid exploitation.

Good objective: cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players (their best response is D, and D,D gives me 1 instead of 0). Treat claims as unverified; track encounter actions.
Defect each round: it gives a higher payoff against either opponent action.

Good players maximize joint good-player payoff: cooperate with likely-good opponents; defect against likely-selfish opponents to avoid 0 against their defection. Track actions and leader claims as evidence, not proof.

P2 untested; cooperate this round, record outcome. Prior conditional on my good role: 0/2/4 selfish among others equally likely (marginal 2/9 each).
P4 defected against my C in round 1; treat as evidence, not proof of selfishness. P5’s public plan is plausible; evaluate its actions independently.
P2 defected against my C; mark suspicious. P10 is untested. For the good-player total, favor C with likely-good opponents and D when selfishness is sufficiently likely; treat claims as unverified.
P1 chose C against my D and earned 0. P3 is untested. As selfish, choose D.

P3 is untested; cooperate to maximize good players’ joint payoff if P3 is good. Update suspicion from the encounter, but don’t infer selfishness from a single action alone.
Continue defecting to maximize my payoff. P5’s public claims concern its own encounters and do not change my action.

P1 is untested; cooperate this round to support mutual cooperation if good. A defection against C is strong evidence of selfishness, though not proof. P9 and P4 defected against me; P2 also defected. P5/P6 cooperated. Treat public claims as unverified.

P6 is untested; cooperate to support mutual welfare if good, then update from their action.

P6 is untested; cooperate unless new evidence makes selfishness more likely than not. Good-good mutual cooperation maximizes their combined payoff; defect only to avoid being exploited by a selfish opponent.
